articles.title: The far right is menacing Europe – but it is fragile. What the extremists and voters want isn’t the same | Gordon Brown
articles.summary:
As Spain heads into a critical election, polling shows that many voters attracted by rightwing parties don’t really agree with their ideas

When Spain goes to the polls on 29 November, its citizens will be the first of some 200 million people in Europe eligible to vote in the following 12 months; 2027 will be a year of elections – including France, Poland, Estonia and Italy – which will be critical to the future of Europe. This will be the biggest electoral test in nearly 100 years of the strength and threat of extreme rightwing populist nationalism.

Thirty years ago, around the turn of the 21st century, the left was ascendant, in charge or in coalition in 13 out of the EU’s 15 member states. Today, with Denmark the only social democratic-led government in the north of Europe, and Lithuania the only one in the east, Spain stands alongside tiny Malta as the only centre-left government in Europe’s south.
